record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: If a complex polynomial P of degree n > 1 shares a root with each derivative P^(k) for k = 1,2,…,n−1, determine whether P must be of the form b(z−a)^n for some complex numbers a and b ≠ 0.

evidence.quote: Problem 30 (Casas-Alvero’s conjecture). If a complex polynomial P of degree n >1 shares roots with all its derivatives, P (k),k = 1, 2...,n−1, then there exist two complex numbers,a and b̸= 0, such that P (z) =b(z−a)n.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let P(z) be a polynomial of degree n > 1 with complex coefficients. For each k = 1, 2, ..., n-1, denote by P^(k) the k-th derivative of P, and suppose that P and P^(k) share at least one common root in the complex numbers (i.e., gcd(P, P^(k)) is nonconstant). Determine whether P must necessarily be of the form P(z) = b(z - a)^n for some complex numbers a and b with b ≠ 0.
artifact.status_search_result: The Casas-Alvero conjecture was historically open and known only for special degrees (e.g., p^k, 2p^k, and certain forms involving small primes). In January 2025, Soham Ghosh posted a preprint claiming a full proof in characteristic zero using Koszul homology, with a revised version in 2026. Since the proof has not yet been independently confirmed/published in a peer-reviewed venue at the time of writing, the conjecture is best classified as partially solved with a claimed full proof under review.

status_evidence.title: Proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture (arXiv:2501.09272)
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture for polynomials of degree d≥3 over any characteristic-0 field via Koszul homology.
status_evidence.claim: A proof of the Casas-Alvero conjecture in characteristic zero has been announced (preprint, January 2025).

status_evidence.title: Casas-Alvero conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture is known to hold in characteristic zero for degrees of the form p^k and 2p^k, etc.
status_evidence.claim: Prior to 2025, only partial results for specific degree classes were known.

status_evidence.title: The Casas-Alvero conjecture for infinitely many degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the conjecture for infinitely many degrees.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results establish the conjecture for infinite families of degrees.
